Simplify phase for BUG-005, executed as bubbles.simplify at HEAD 363effa64, scoped to the code the fix commit 732bccb6c actually changed: the ~20-line relocation inside deriveInterestSignals in rlportfolio.js. Full evidence at report.md#simplify-phase-2026-08-25. This is a cleanup verdict, not certification and not a re-proof of the fix. Working-tree state was disclosed rather than assumed clean: the same seven framework-install files recorded as REG-B005-R2 were modified at entry and remain so at exit, none of them product source or a Feature 008 artifact, and rlportfolio.js was clean at entry. VERDICT MINIMAL: the fix needed no structural change. It moves the bucket literal and nothing else, carries a why-comment at the point of the hazard, and introduces no duplication, no dead code, and no missing abstraction. Three candidate simplifications were examined against source and REJECTED on the record rather than applied to manufacture activity. First, the duplicated age expression at rlportfolio.js:2462 and :2485 is a structurally NECESSARY recompute, not a defect: dedupeBehaviorEvents sits between the two loops, so accumulating score in the filter loop would count pre-collapse repeats and inflate every domain, leaving only cosmetic extraction of a one-line expression used twice inside one function, which is a stylistic preference rather than an evidence-driven change; the third 86400000 at :2520 adds the retention window to derive expiresAt and is a different operation. Second, moving var byDomain below the filter loop was rejected because var is function-scoped and hoisted, so the name stays in lexical scope either way and the move buys only a runtime TypeError while reading as a stranded declaration in a deliberately ES5/UMD no-build file. Third, no dead code exists: inputCount, retainedCount and collapsedCount are asserted by tests/portfolio-foundation.unit.mjs:631-643 and the function is exported at :4949 and consumed by three carriers. Cross-module reuse was NOT merged, deliberately: rlportfoliobrief.js:331 defines its own dedupeBehaviorEvents with a different signature and contract (BehaviorInterestSignal/v1 versus portfolio-interest-signal/v1), and the comment at rlportfoliobrief.js:493 records why hoisting validatePolicy would change which refusal a doubly-invalid policy reports, so that divergence is intentional under BUG-004 and merging is not recommended. Two things were genuinely wrong and WERE fixed. (1) The comment the fix introduced said expiresAt 'becomes an invalid date'; it does not, it throws, which was measured rather than asserted: new Date(Date.parse(null) + 30*86400000).toISOString() raises RangeError: Invalid time value with Date.parse(null) = NaN. The distinction matters because the bug's entire severity is that it crashes, and a reader who believes the failure merely emits a bad string could reasonably relax the guard. The correction is one comment-only line, zero behavior change. (2) This packet's own report.md was breaking the canonical repository selftest, which was RED at entry at 3410 passed 1 failed, exit 1. The cause was named from the guard's own output rather than inferred: validateSpecTestPaths reported exactly one newMissing entry — the carrier name the dispatch used, under tests/, which this note deliberately does not spell in full for the same reason the finding describes — sited at report.md line 1043. That guard reads spec artifacts and the tests/ tree and never opens rlportfolio.js, so the comment edit was causally excluded rather than assumed innocent. Line 1043 was the regression phase's own prose correctly disclosing that the dispatch had misnamed the carrier; the disclosure is true and was KEPT, and what broke the gate was writing the absent name as a live repo-root tests/*.mjs token, which TEST_PATH_TOKEN at validate-spec-test-paths.mjs:60 reads as a claim that the file exists. The prose now states the same fact without the path prefix and explains why, so a later editor does not restore it and re-break the gate; no true information was deleted to make a gate green. Stabilize phase for BUG-005, recorded at HEAD e4c97ca9b. Full evidence at report.md#stabilize-phase-2026-08-25. VERDICT STABLE: no performance regression is attributable to BUG-005. PROVENANCE IS DECLARED RATHER THAN BLURRED, and this is the single most important qualification on the record. This invocation PERSISTS a measurement taken in a prior invocation; it did not re-establish one, because the fixture build costs about four minutes and the operator directed that it not be re-run. Consequently every millisecond figure, ratio, signals count, heap delta and refusal code in the section is graded interpreted, NOT executed: this agent did not run the harness in this session and does not hold the raw captured stdout, so those numbers are operator-transcribed diagnostic input and are labelled as such rather than restated as this agent's own execution evidence. What this agent DID execute and can show is the setup integrity, which is what makes the transcribed numbers mean anything: harness /tmp/stab-b005/bench.mjs sha256 24ea33c1bc1e7e984bd00b387a0ff794eb9fa63316b18d9a4b5dcacf534fb345; pre-fix worktree /tmp/stab-b005-pre at 31aad20d4; node v22.22.0 on 8 cores; and a diff proving the ONLY divergence between the two sides of rlportfolio.js is the BUG-005 hunk itself, one statement reordering that moves bucket creation after the age filter and adds no per-event work, so any measured delta is attributable to this change or to nothing. Method read from harness source rather than assumed: one fixture serves all three age regimes by varying now, each figure is the median of 21 timed repetitions after 3 warm-ups, and pre and post are interleaved inside one process so drift hits both sides equally; maxBehaviorEvents is 500 and maximumEvidenceAgeDays is 56. RESULTS at n=500 for portfolio.deriveInterestSignals: fresh, 500 of 500 in-window across 4 domains, pre 724.8 ms versus post 867.0 ms, ratio 1.196, output IDENTICAL at signals=4; mixed, 327 of 500 across 4 domains, pre 767.8 ms versus post 697.6 ms, ratio 0.909, output IDENTICAL at signals=4; stale, 0 of 500 across 0 domains, pre THREW RangeError Invalid time value while post returned ok in 519.5 ms at signals=0. The stale row has NO ratio and cannot have one, and that is not a measurement failure: the pre side throwing IS the defect this bug repairs, reproduced a third time in a different harness on a different path than the unit carrier, so a stale-only workspace simply has no pre-fix runtime to compare against. The two comparable regimes produce byte-identical output, so the repair changes cost only and never result. The two ratios point in OPPOSITE directions, 1.196 and 0.909, for a change that adds no per-event work, which is the signature of noise rather than effect. That reading is not asserted, it is bounded from the data: n=500 fresh was measured twice, at pre 724.8 post 867.0 ratio 1.196 in the regime block and at pre 890.8 post 700.9 ratio 0.787 in the scaling block, so the same function over the same fixture varies by roughly plus or minus 20 percent in BOTH directions, a spread wider than either observed pre/post gap, which places the 1.196 inside the noise band where it cannot be read as a regression. Scaling in the fresh regime, n=50 pre 93.4 post 112.9 and n=500 pre 890.8 post 700.9, so 10x the events scales time by pre 9.53x versus post 6.21x and the post side scales BETTER, consistent with filtering before allocating. Cap enforcement at n=501 still refuses rather than degrades: both sides reject with the same P008-SCHEMA-CORRUPT and behavior-event-cap-exceeded, pre 0.8 ms and post 0.7 ms, so the repair did not convert a short-circuit refusal into slow work. Retained growth across 200 consecutive post-fix calls at n=500 shows heapUsed deltas straddling zero, fresh +0.05 MiB, mixed +0.03 MiB, stale -0.04 MiB, and output length bounded by DOMAIN COUNT at 4, 4 and 0 rather than by n, which is the structural reason a stale regime returns an empty list instead of allocating four dead buckets and is the same property the repair relies on. TWO CAVEATS ARE STATED EXPLICITLY AND MUST TRAVEL WITH THESE NUMBERS. CAVEAT 1: BUG-004's recorded 201 ms baseline is for brief.deriveInterestSignals in rlportfoliobrief.js, a DIFFERENT function from the rlportfolio.deriveInterestSignals changed here; they share a name and nothing else, having different modules, signatures and contracts, BehaviorInterestSignal/v1 versus portfolio-interest-signal/v1, as the simplify phase already established when it declined to merge them, so comparing this section's roughly 700 to 900 ms against 201 ms would compare two unrelated functions and manufacture a regression that does not exist. The BUG-004 function was measured here for exactly that reason and came back 303.6 ms post versus 307.7 ms pre, ratio 0.987, UNCHANGED by this repair. Note also that BUG-004's own packet carries an identically named stabilize-phase-2026-08-25 anchor, which is a different packet's section and not this one. CAVEAT 2: absolute milliseconds were taken on a machine at loadavg 13.90 across 8 cores, roughly 1.7x oversubscribed, so every absolute figure is inflated by contention from unrelated concurrent work and is NOT comparable to numbers recorded on an idle machine; absolute ms must not be quoted as a latency budget, compared against a quiet-machine figure, or used to set a threshold. The load-independent evidence the verdict actually rests on is the pre/post ratios, which are interleaved inside one process so contention hits both sides equally, the byte-identical outputs in the two comparable regimes, the identical refusal code at the cap, and the non-accumulating heap deltas. Working-tree state was disclosed rather than assumed clean: the same seven framework-install files recorded as REG-B005-R2 remain modified, none of them product source or a Feature 008 artifact, and rlportfolio.js was clean.
